text:
Ari Patel: Quick sync — we're finalizing the cost model inputs from hardware partners next week. Need the following per-SKU from each vendor: reserved price (1/12/36mo), spot average price, historical eviction rate by region, any latency or priority premiums (e.g., +% for guaranteed p99 latency tiers), marketplace listing fees, and credit/payment terms. Can partners share a sample CSV schema? cc @Ming Zhou

Ming Zhou: Pinged VegaCompute & CoreCloud earlier today. Vega replied with a high-level CSV and some verbal notes. CoreCloud said they'll send a cleaned CSV by EOD Fri. Quick highlights from Vega: spot eviction ~3-5% monthly for eu-west, ~1-2% in us-west; they charge a +10% "latency premium" for guaranteed p99 <50ms on 4k-context SKUs. They also have a marketplace listing fee of 2.5% or a flat $4k/month for large partners. Link they shared: https://files.vega/sku-sample.csv (internal)

Sasha Kim: For finance modelling — how do vendors define SLA credits? Are they flat credits on invoices, or pro-rated refunds? need exact wording to model downside. Also, do any vendors have minimum monthly billing floors that break our per-token assumptions?

Ming Zhou: Vega's term (paraphrased): "SLA credit issued as invoice credit; 5% monthly credit if monthly uptime <99%; 10% credit if uptime <97%; escalator applies at account level for repeat misses." CoreCloud uses a sliding scale plus the option to apply credits against future reserved commitments. Also flagged: some vendors will apply a minimum billing floor for reserved pools < 10 devices.

Devon Cruz: Two product asks: 1) add a latency_premium column per SKU in the CSV so we can calculate blended cost when customers request higher QoS; 2) include a commit_conversion_discount (vendors sometimes give conversion discounts when reserved capacity converts to on-demand or vice versa). That'll let us simulate fallbacks in routing policies.

Ming Zhou: Copying a sanitized sample Vega CSV payload they sent (trimmed):

```
sku,region,device_type,reserved_1mo,reserved_12mo,reserved_36mo,spot_avg,spot_eviction_pct,latency_premium_pct,marketplace_fee_pct,min_billing_floor
vc-gpu-a100-80,us-west,nvidia_a100_80,10.50,9.00,7.50,3.25,1.5,10,2.5,10000
vc-gpu-a100-80,eu-west,nvidia_a100_80,11.20,9.80,8.00,3.10,3.8,10,2.5,10000
vc-gpu-h100-80,us-west,nvidia_h100,18.00,15.50,13.00,5.50,2.0,12,3.0,20000
```

Ming Zhou: Also attached (uploaded) vendor file names to the channel: VendorBot: uploaded vega-sku-sample.csv

VendorBot: vega-sku-sample.csv uploaded by Ming Zhou — link: https://internal.storage/vega-sku-sample.csv

Sasha Kim: Good. For modelling scenarios I'll build three: 1) high-reserved (70% reserved mix), 2) balanced (40% reserved), 3) low-reserved (10% reserved, high spot). For each, I'll include percentile eviction shocks (+50% eviction) and marketplace fee sensitivity (+/- 1.5%). Will share baseline numbers tomorrow.

Maria Lopez: Ops note — marketplace listing fees often include a separate "fulfillment" surcharge for cross-region traffic that vendors don't always disclose up front. I've seen extra network/egress adders of 0.5-1.2% depending on partner. Also some partners include a 30-day payment net + early-pay discounts (1.5%).

Devon Cruz: Can we add two more columns to the CSV request: "cross_region_egress_pct" and "early_pay_discount_pct"? that'll keep the billing calc honest.

Ari Patel: Action items: Ming to collect final CSVs from Vega, CoreCloud, and Zenith by Fri COB (Ming). Sasha to produce three scenario runs and a short deck with sensitivity tables (Sasha). Devon to update the modelling template with latency_premium, commit_conversion_discount, cross_region_egress_pct, early_pay_discount_pct (Devon). Maria to collate any hidden fee examples from ops/support (Maria). We'll use this to finalize partner negotiation asks next week. :thumbsup:

Ming Zhou: on it. I'll thread vendor legal on any SLAs that look non-standard.

Sasha Kim: I'll aim to share the google sheet & quick chart tomorrow morning.

Devon Cruz: I'll add a column for "fallback_variant_sku" so routing can model automatic downgrade when reserved pool unavailable.

Ari Patel: Thanks everyone — please drop any vendor redlines or non-standard billing terms into this thread so finance/legal can triage.
